title: Establishing the Kingdom and Preparing Defenses
summary: The people begin to establish the kingdom and possess the land in peace. The narrator has weapons made and sets guards around the land to protect the people and flocks.

explicit_facts.text: The people begin to establish the kingdom and possess the land in peace.
The narrator has weapons of war made for the people in preparation for a possible Lamanite attack.
The narrator sets guards around the land to protect the people and flocks.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People making weapons and guards stationed around the land may be shown.
unspecified_visual_details: The land's name and appearance, the weapons' designs, and the guards' number and appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: we again began to establish the kingdom
I set guards round about the land

prohibited_inventions: Do not name the narrator or the land.
Do not depict a Lamanite attack as occurring in this scene.

title: Years of Peaceful Inheritance
summary: For twenty-two years, the people inherited their fathers’ land. Men tilled the ground and raised grain and fruit; women spun and made linen and cloth. The people prospered and had continual peace.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator’s people inherited the land of their fathers for twenty-two years.
The narrator caused the men to till the ground and raise grain and fruit.
The narrator caused the women to spin and make fine linen and cloth.
The people prospered and had continual peace in the land for twenty-two years.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Agricultural work and textile-making may be depicted as activities during this period, without presenting the twenty-two years as a single instant.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific crops, tools, garments, buildings, and individual appearances are not specified.

narration.text: for the space of twenty and two years
the men should till the ground
the women should spin, and toil, and work

prohibited_inventions: Do not name the narrator or the people, or identify the land as Shilom.
Do not present the twenty-two years as one moment or invent events within them.

title: King Laman’s Son Begins to Reign
summary: King Laman dies. His son begins to reign, stirs his people to rebellion against the narrator’s people, and they begin to prepare for war and come up to battle.

explicit_facts.text: King Laman died, and his son began to reign in his stead.
His son began to stir his people up in rebellion against the narrator’s people.
His people began to prepare for war and come up to battle against the narrator’s people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The son’s reign and his people’s preparations may be represented without depicting an unmentioned ceremony or specific speech.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, the son’s name and appearance, and the methods of preparation are not specified.

narration.text: king Laman died
his son began to reign in his stead.
they began to prepare for war, and to come up to battle against my people.

prohibited_inventions: Do not name the son or place these events in Shemlon.
Do not add a coronation, speech, or the daughters of the Lamanites.

summary: Zeniff’s spies are sent around Shemlon to discover the enemy’s preparations.

explicit_facts.text: Zeniff has sent spies around Shemlon to discover preparations and guard against an attack.

narration.text: I had sent my spies out round about the land of Shemlon

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the spies witnessing a specific conversation or event not stated in the verse.

title: The Lamanites’ Inherited Belief
summary: Zeniff recounts the Lamanites’ belief that their ancestors were wronged and driven from the land, connecting it to Nephi’s greater faithfulness and the Lord’s favor.

explicit_facts.text: Zeniff describes the Lamanites as believing they were driven from Jerusalem for their fathers’ iniquities and wronged in the wilderness and while crossing the sea.
They also believe they were wronged in their first inheritance after crossing the sea, because Nephi was more faithful, favored by the Lord, and led their journey in the wilderness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The passage reports an inherited belief and historical claims; it does not narrate these past events as occurring in the present.
unspecified_visual_details: No present-day visible action or location is supplied for this account.

narration.text: they were wronged in the wilderness by their brethren
they were also wronged while crossing the sea
Nephi was more faithful in keeping the commandments of the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are reported beliefs and historical narration, not a visual reenactment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the journey, sea crossing, or Nephi’s leadership as events happening now.

title: Anger After Arrival
summary: After arriving in the promised land, his brethren were angry with him. They said he had taken the ruling of the people out of their hands, and they sought to kill him.

explicit_facts.text: His brethren were angry with him after they arrived in the promised land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The brethren and the man they were angry with may be shown after their arrival.
unspecified_visual_details: Their appearances and the precise setting are not specified.

narration.text: And again, they were wroth with him when they had arrived in the promised land, because they said that he had taken the ruling of the people out of their hands; and they sought to kill him.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mosiah 10:14 refers to anger upon the waters at a separate time; Mosiah 10:16 refers to anger over his departure into the wilderness with the records at another time. Neither event is part of this scene.
The accusation is reported, not supplied as direct speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the events upon the waters or the departure into the wilderness as occurring in this scene.
Do not invent dialogue, an attack, names, or an appearance of the Lord.
